_doc: Abyssfire VFX recipes, art pass (Art/blender/vfx/fx_recipes.py). Schema: Source/Abyssfire/Public/World/WorldContract.md 5 / AbyssVfxRecipe.h; merged over the runtime's built-in defaults (same id replaces). Textures T_FX_<sprite> are linear RGBA (sRGB off): RGB tints, A coverage; the Flame, ShardFrost, Arrow, Coin, Rock and Chain cells are pre-coloured (white tint). Meshes SM_FX_* are drawn by M_AF_FX_Mesh (one tint per particle, toon bands, ink hull, AF_Data.a value channel).

ambient.ashfall.note: falling ash (chapter1.md §15 march mood): 28 flakes + 30 specks per second over a 9 m disc round the hero, falling 35-60 cm/s with a drift along world +X (~120 + ~140 alive); the weather tint (#CFCAC0) colours them

ambient.sparks.note: motes rising: the embers palette's mid (#FF6A3A, the abyss_rift ember storm) without a context colour; the weather tint when the runtime passes it (the Breach Rim region: #B02FD0); 8-13 cm points, not blobs

camp.bell_toll.note: the keepers' bell tolls (story beats; U4 / U7 bell cue at the bell frame's `bell` socket): slow, soft pale tones in the air at the bell, a faint swell over the ground, ash shaken off the frame — no violet (the bell is the living's), no warm light (the lantern is the frame's own); the hostile clapper slam (notify.FX_BellRing) is a fast cracked dust ring instead

camp.hearthstone.note: NS_World_Hearthstone (forward-compatible id: the world builder can play it at camp hearthstones)

camp.torch@march.note: the march brazier's smoulder (SM_Prop_March_Brazier, camp_torch@march): grey-brown smoke curling up, a few dull red sparks (#7A3420, below the ember band) and ash flakes off the bed; NO light (chapter1.md §15 reserved light). Runtime: EffectSpots must resolve camp.torch@<zone theme> before camp.torch (U1)

corpse.burn.note: U3: a fire killing blow / fire over a corpse burns it (unraisable): a flare in the fire's own colour (event: the hero's fire orange, breach fire violet; grey without one), soot, ash

corpse.consume.note: U3: a gravegnawer tearing at a husk for 2 s (Consume; origin = the gnawer beside it, Blow = gnawer -> husk): pale ash, flakes and grit tossed up and back at its jaws, in front of the body (spawned inside the slumped husk they never drew)

corpse.crumble.note: U3: the body greys and slumps into an ash husk — ash dust spreading low, flakes falling off it

corpse.expire.note: U3: the husk's TTL ends — the ash lifts and blows away along world +X

death.breach.note: breach-blood bursts: tar flung, violet sparks; then the tar puddle (runtime fx.puddle) dries in 3 s

death.cinderbloat.note: a cinderbloat is killed (death.<defId>): a dull crust crack and an ash puff only — the fuse (notify.FX_Fuse) and the burst (notify.FX_Burst @800) are its death; no tar, no violet

death.gravegnawers.note: a Gravegnawer falls: dust and ash flecks off the hide, a puff as it drops (beasts: no violet)

death.living.note: a Living enemy falls: dust off the blow, then a slap of mud as the body lands; no light, no blood (ash mode)

death.unburied.note: an Unburied falls: a violet breath leaves through the head, the pinpoints go out, ash puffs off the folding body; no blood

death.valdras.note: Valdras falls (death.<defId>, actor frame: Blow = his facing): violet guttering out of the standard along its droop (upright → falling → drooped) and out of the seams for ~1.6 s, two fine ripples, dust as he kneels (Kneel 1100 ms)

elite.curse_aura.note: Dirgecursed (哀咒): bell ripples rolling out to the r4 aura edge (Ripple, violet-grey), a dark haze

elite.extra_strong.note: Brutish (蛮力): weight — an iron-dark disc with a held crack mark, a pale ash heartbeat rim, dust and grit shoved off the feet; no crimson (the telegraph's colour), no orange

elite.fire_enhanced.note: Scorched (焦灼): breach fire at the feet (violet-black tongues on a soot disc), violet motes; never ember

elite.fire_enhanced.death.note: Scorched (焦灼) on death (W2): the corpse smoulders with breach fire for 1 s (U2's elite-style crimson r2 decal fills over the same second), then a breach-fire burst at r2 — flames on a ring, an ash shock ring, violet cracks in a scorch, ash thrown

elite.frozen.note: Gravecold (墓寒): grey-blue rime crusting at the feet, cold breath rising, frozen ash falling (desaturated: the hero's ice is the saturated blue)

elite.frozen.death.note: Gravecold (墓寒) on death (W2): grey-blue rime fades in over the r2.5 zone and cold mist draws in (the pre-cue), at 600 ms a grave-cold ring snaps out and the frost crust holds for the 2.5 s slow; no crimson (a slow, not damage: DR5)

elite.swift.note: Driven (驱策): a pale wind swirl spinning at the feet (Swirl, ash white over a dark under-swirl) and dust whipped round (grey; no colour of its own)

elite.teleporting.note: Breachwalker (渊行): the body smears through space — big flickering violet tears beside it (no rim ring: the tears lead) — and winking wisps; the blink itself is teleport.blink

elite.unburied.note: Unburied (不葬, forward-compatible: the affix is W2 data): violet cracks under the feet, motes seeping up

elite.vampiric.note: Breach-Drinker (噬渊): a near-black tar disc (maroon drops read as blood); big tar drops and violet motes spiral in and up, a dull tar-violet hairline contracts onto the body (the other auras breathe out)

hazard.banner_ring.note: P3's closing banner ring (W2 EvArena): breach fire round the ring's edge (unit radius = the arena's current radius; re-play as it shrinks); the damage side (outside: 4 % max life / s) is U2's arena-style crimson decal (TELEGRAPH styles.arena), not this recipe

hazard.breach_fire.note: a burning brand / breach-fire patch (W2 EvHazard, unit radius): violet cracks in a scorch, breach fire licking up

hazard.breach_seep.note: 渗裂 Breach-seep (W2): a crack line (origin → target, 8 × 1 tiles) splitting in violet, breach fire along it for the two ticks; the crimson line stays on through the ticks (U2: the windup's decal hands over to the hazard style at contact until the zone ends — TELEGRAPH styles.hazard)

monster.ash_flakes.note: a monster loop (cinderbloat fx.ashFlakes): ash drifting off the crust from its vent, a rare violet spit

monster.block.note: EvBlock (W2): steel on the tower shield — a bone-white arc across the blow, pale sparks thrown back at the attacker, a dull clang ring (no orange)

monster.dead_standard_bearer.aura.note: the dead standard-bearer's +15 % aura (W2, r 5 tiles, loop on the bearer while it lives): a soft cloth-dark crimson stain breathing on the ground, ash drifting off the banner over it — no rim line, no fill sweep, never the telegraph crimson (DR5)

monster.oath_zealot.frenzy.note: the zealot's frenzy loop (W2: EvMonsterPhase zealot index 1 until death; Blow = his facing): panting breath out of the hood — a pale cloud always before the hood, the frenzy's persistent read (the scar is ~1 px at 1080p) — and dust kicked at his feet; no light (the Living carry none)

monster.raise.mark.note: the raise marker (W2): a breach-violet ring of grasping fingers closing on the corpse over 900 ms, violet motes drawn in; then monster.raise as it stands

monster.valdras.feed.note: Feed (W2): the corpse's ash streams into the standard as violet streaks; Valdras heals (the gather sits over his head: Blow runs corpse -> Valdras, not along his facing, so a back offset would drift)

monster.valdras.standard_fire.note: Valdras P3 No Retreat (W2): breach fire burning up the standard, violet motes and soot streaming off

notify.FX_BannerSnap.note: the banner snapping in a wind that isn't there: ash shaken off the cloth

notify.FX_BellRing.note: the Clapper Slam: an impact — a fast dust ring hugging the ground, the ground split, thick dust and grit (no bell ripple: that is the keepers' camp.bell_toll; the Gravegnawers are beasts, not breach-touched: no violet)

notify.FX_BellToll.note: the Corpseherd's bell-toll bolt leaving the bell (the bolt is proj.monster_bolt, #B02FD0)

notify.FX_Brand.note: the Oath-Brand slam: the ground splits in violet light round the planted blade, breach fire erupts on a ring; the 4 s burning brand is hazard.breach_fire

notify.FX_Burst.note: cinderbloat Death @800 ms: the burst — violet-black flame ring, a soot blast, an ash shock ring, cracks glowing violet in a scorch, ash thrown and settling; no gore

notify.FX_Dig.note: the burial detail digging a grave that is no longer there: clods and dust

notify.FX_DrumBeat_1.note: a drum beat: dust off the drum head and a faint pale beat ripple; no light

notify.FX_Frenzy.note: the zealot's frenzy (W2, Roar FX_Frenzy @480): the chant breaks out of the hood as a pale breath, dust shoved off his feet, ash shaken off the whipping robe — no light (the scar flare is fx.frenzy's material parameter)

notify.FX_Fuse.note: cinderbloat Death @0 → 800 ms: the fuse — light swelling from below, violet spits, ash shaken off the crust, a ring tightening (the crimson r2.2 hazard ring is U2's telegraph, not this recipe)

notify.FX_Keen.note: the Corpseherd's Keen (W2 stretch, Cast02 FX_Keen @800): the lament breaks out — violet sound rings before the veil (the voice, slower), a hairline ripple sweeping the ground to r 4 m in 220 ms and flaring at the rim (everyone inside is slowed at 800), the ash blown outward; the crimson ring is U2's telegraph decal (filled to its rim at 800), the slow is status.slow

notify.FX_Land.note: a hop landing: a dull dust pat (no colour: the clot's sparks are its own emissive)

notify.FX_Roar.note: Valdras' Roar: a dust shock at his feet, a pale shout, and breach fire flaring up the standard (its P3 burning is monster.valdras.standard_fire). The goblin chief's Roar (later chapters) reuses the notify name

notify.FX_bell_ring.note: Call the Flock (召羊): the bell's toll as violet ripples — in the air at the bell, two rolling out over the ground toward the 6-tile call (r 3.8 m shown)

npc.FX_HammerStrike.note: NS_NPC_AnvilSparks: Work_Hammer notify FX_HammerStrike (426.6 ms) at SM_Prop_Camp_AnvilStump `strike`

skill.fireball.note: cast glint only: the flight is proj.fireball(.launch / .hit)

skill.meteor.note: the impact shake fires at +300 (combat-feel: at impact) — the recipe shake starts with the cast; the runtime's impact hook may replace it

skill.multishot.note: 7 arrows fanned evenly over ±46° (±0.8 rad) round the aim (`fan`: particle i of N at yaw cone·((i + .5) / N − .5); runtimes without it draw the random ±46° cone), 3.3 tiles in 220 ms (the web's fallback fan); gravity offsets the blow direction's random climb so the volley lands level

skill.piercing_arrow.note: the line (6 tiles) is drawn along the blow; three shock rings mark ¼ ½ ¾ as the arrow passes

status.ashnumb.note: 麻灰 Ashnumb (W2, K6): ash flaking off the hero's limbs and settling at the feet; the grey band creeping up the limbs per stack is the StatusTint contract dark.materials.AshnumbTint (runtime)

status.bleed.note: optional R8 bleed visual: a held wound, blood drips + spatters round the feet; StatusTint #C8323C α .22

status.burn.note: R8 burn embers: 2–3 small cel flames + embers + a warm ground glow; StatusTint #FF7A3A α .35

status.freeze.note: R8 frost crystals at the feet (SM_FX_FrostCrust) + a frosted veil; StatusTint #7FD0FF α .45

status.slow.note: optional R8 slow visual: a frost swirl at the feet

status.stun.note: R8 stun stars: toon stars orbiting fx_overhead, facing the W1 camera

telegraph.contact.note: the telegraph's contact beat (W2, U2): a crimson rim snap and dust at the rim; scaled by the radius

telegraph.contact.cone.note: a cone telegraph's contact (W2): a fan of dust and crimson spits along the blow

telegraph.contact.line.note: a line telegraph's contact (W2): dust and crimson spits along origin → target

teleport.blink.note: the elite blink (渊行 Breachwalker): a violet smear along the path, soot where it left, wisps where it lands

integration.groundSoftFade: M_AF_FX_Sprite fades every quad with DepthFade(8 cm) and the runtime has no ground special case, so every ground-oriented sprite quad (rings, shocks, decals, runes, pools, auras) is authored 8-10 cm over the terrain (fx_recipes.ground_lift; full strength from 6.2 cm at the W1 pitch). The previews draw exactly the shipped 8 cm fade on every quad. The runtime's fake light pools (UAbyssVfxSystem lights, +2 cm) and the prop pools (AAbyssPropActor, M_AF_LightPool) still sit at 2 cm and draw at ~25 %: lift them to 8 cm too (or skip DepthFade for ground quads / M_AF_LightPool).
integration.fan: Layer key `fan` (bool, dir blow / back): particle i of a burst of N flies at yaw cone*((i + 0.5) / N - 0.5) round the axis instead of a random yaw in the cone - an even fan (skill.multishot: 7 arrows over the web's +-0.8 rad). Needs FAbyssVfxLayer::bFan + ReadBool("fan") + the Serial-based yaw in SpawnParticle; until then the runtime ignores the key (random cone).
integration.dirBlowPitch: EAbyssVfxDir::Blow adds Direction.Z = rand(-0.15, 0.35): the arrow / shard heads (proj.arrow / multishot / poison_arrow / ice_arrow / piercing_arrow) are 60 /s copies living 90 ms, flat on the ground plane and turned to the flight (orient ground + alignToBlow; UpdateProjectiles turns Context.Blow to the heading), so no copy takes a random pitch and the head is gone <= 75 ms after HandleProjectileEnded's Stop(handle, false) instead of a count-1 particle parked in the target for the rest of its 520 ms (VFX review 4). No runtime change needed.
integration.flat: Layer key `flat` (bool, dir blow / back): Direction.Z = 0 instead of rand(-0.15, 0.35) - a level free flight. Needs FAbyssVfxLayer::bFlat + ReadBool("flat") + `Direction.Z = Layer.bFlat ? 0.f : Random.FRandRange(-0.15f, 0.35f)` in SpawnParticle; until then the runtime ignores the key. Used by proj.piercing_arrow.hit (the arrow flying on through its target, spec 8.6; forward-compatible: no core projectile carries vfxId piercing_arrow today) and recommended for skill.piercing_arrow's arrow + comet (drop their gravityCmS2 1100 then).
integration.hitImpactProfiles: hit.impact.<light|normal|heavy|crit|kill> differ beyond ring size / spark count (light: lower core / glow / ring alpha, 4 short slow sparks - VFX review 4). The runtime plays hit.impact today: PlayFirst({hit.impact.<profile>, hit.impact}) with the HitFeedback weight name is the one-line change; the previews play the profile ids.
integration.meshMaterial: mesh layers always draw M_AF_FX_Mesh (opaque masked toon + ink, Bayer fade) — glow, smoke and energy stay sprites; ribbons / crystals / plates / debris / heads are meshes.
integration.bodyOcclusion: Sprites are depth-tested against the opaque characters, and a chest / head anchor is the fx_chest / fx_head socket = the middle of the body, so a burst centred there loses everything inside the silhouette (the web drew FX over its sprites). The strike recipes pull their target-side burst layers 22 cm back along the blow (onto the struck surface, fx_recipes.STRIKE_CM); a burst struck from behind the target (attacker farther from the camera) is still partly hidden. Recommended runtime fix: billboard / velocity layers anchored on an actor (origin / target / point at chest, head, hand or overhead) move their quad toward the camera by min(40 cm, 0.5 x the actor's capsule radius + 20 cm) (Position -= CameraForward * Bias in UAbyssVfxSystem::Tick, or a camera-ward WPO in M_AF_FX_Additive / _Translucent) - at the W1 distance that is <2 % size change.
integration.cameraBias: Blow-less recipes (level-up, pickups, statuses, loot, portal, resonance, props, camps) carry offsetCm d*(-0.455, -0.455, +0.766) with d = 40 cm on their body-anchored quads: with the zero blow the frame is world +X/+Y and the W1 yaw is fixed, so that is the view ray toward the camera (same screen position, drawn over the body). Re-derive (fx_recipes.CAM_BIAS_CM) if the camera yaw ever changes or these events get a blow.
integration.loopPrewarm: Rate emitters start empty (first particle after 1000 / rate ms). Loop layers slower than 3 /s carry a one-particle burst copy (count 1) so a status / prop loop shows at once (fx_recipes.prewarm).
integration.perClassBasic: hit.basic.<class> and hit.impact.<profile> are authored for a one-line runtime change (PlayFirst({hit.basic.<class>, hit.basic}) / ({hit.impact.<profile>, hit.impact})).
integration.elite: elite.<affix> and camp.hearthstone are forward-compatible ids (not bound to events yet).
integration.lootBeam: loot.beam.<magic|rare|legendary|set> are LOOPS for the loot prop (WorldContract 5.3: add a 'GroundItem prop loop' row): in UAbyssWorldBuilder::SpawnEntity's GroundItem branch set LoopRecipe = loot.beam.<quality> for quality >= Magic (Normal: none). The prop's vfx:<handle> tag already stops it in RemoveEntity on pickup / despawn. loot.drop.* stay the drop-moment burst; the 31 cm PoolRadiusCm light pool can stay (the beam carries its own pool).
integration.clueYaw: SM_FX_ClueMagnifier's lens is tilted back 40 deg and faces the W1 camera at mesh yaw camera + 90 (UE 135 deg; n.v = 0.985); the random Pickup yaw (AbyssWorldBuilder.cpp Setup.YawDeg = TileHash % 360) turns it edge-on. For DefId quest_clue set Setup.YawDeg = CameraYawDeg + 180 (= 225; AAbyssPropActor adds MeshYawOffsetDeg -90 -> mesh yaw 135) + a hash jitter of at most +-8 deg.
integration.chestOpen: prop.chest.open is timed from the start of the chest's Open clip (its layers wait for the ChestOpen notify, 120 ms); nothing plays it yet - play it where the chest prop starts Open (UAbyssWorldBuilder::RemoveEntity, PickedUp / Collected of a Chest-style prop).
integration.meshDissolve: FX mesh layers fade by a 4x4 Bayer screen-door (M_AF_FX_Mesh opacity mask) that TAA / TSR resolves; without TAA (mobile low) any alpha < 31/32 shows as checker noise. The recipes now hold every mesh layer's dithered window (fade-in + late dissolve) to <= 34 ms = 2 frames at 60 Hz (fx_recipes.mesh_dissolve raises alphaPow / cuts fadeIn; at alphaPow 10-12 the shatter / bubble / band dissolves still dithered for 90-190 ms), and rock debris / ice shards no longer dissolve at all (alpha 1, late shrink: grow x .15, sizePow .3). Optional runtime polish: on tiers without TAA use a plain alpha-test at 0.5 instead of the dither.
integration.launchSocket: Projectiles and `hand` layers resolve fx_hand_r. The mage holds the staff there: at Cast01's release the staff crystal is 73 cm further along the cast. Spec 8.1 launches from the crystal: AAbyssCharacterActor::GetAnchorLocation(HandR) returns the main-hand mesh's `crystal` socket when it has one (the previews draw it so).
integration.impactShake: meteor / fireball shakes belong to the impact (combat-feel 11.5); recipe shakes start with the recipe, so the impact recipes (proj.fireball.hit) carry them.
integration.deathFamily: Monster kills play PlayFirst({death.<defId>, death.<family>, death.burst}) instead of death.burst (UAbyssVfxSystem::HandleHit): the march families get their own ends (unburied / breach: violet; living / gravegnawers: dust and ash, no light); keep the event colour #FF4444 for the fallback only. The death ids play anchored to the dying actor: Context.Blow = the victim's facing at death (as PlayNotify), not killer -> victim, so death.valdras' offsets stay on the standard on his back whatever side the kill came from (hit.impact.kill and the death.burst fallback keep the hit's blow). A def whose manifest fx has a fuse (the cinderbloat) has its own quiet death.<defId> (death.cinderbloat): its Death notifies FX_Fuse @0 / FX_Burst @800 are the death, and the family burst at the kill would read as burst -> fuse -> second burst (monsters.md 1.3)
integration.ambienceTint: Play ambient.<ambience> with Context.Color = the zone weather's tint when it has one (ashfall #CFCAC0; the Breach Rim's sparks #B02FD0): both recipes draw the event colour, and without a tint ambient.sparks keeps its ember motes (abyss_rift)
integration.notifyPerMonster: notify.FX_Roar is shared by Valdras and the old goblin chief; a per-asset chain PlayFirst({notify.<SK name>.<N>, notify.<N>, npc.<N>}) would let later chapters give the chief its own
integration.monsterLoops: Start monster.ash_flakes on spawn for monsters whose manifest fx has ashFlakes (the cinderbloat), stop it on death
integration.telegraph: M_AF_Telegraph (dark.materials.M_AF_Telegraph): circle / cone / line / ring, normal / elite / boss / hazard styles; play telegraph.contact[.line|.cone] at contact
integration.ashDissolve: M_AF_AshDissolve (dark.materials.M_AF_AshDissolve) + corpse.* recipes on the husk timeline
integration.eliteDeath: W2 on-death affix effects: play elite.<affix>.death (elite.fire_enhanced.death, elite.frozen.death) at the kill beside death.<family>, point = the corpse; the recipe carries the delay (burst +1000 ms, ring +600 ms), the core resolves the damage / slow at the same beat, and U2 draws the Scorched burst's r2 decal in the elite style
integration.monsterAuras: W2 aura loops: monster.dead_standard_bearer.aura on the bearer (origin, attach) while it lives (stop on death); no telegraph decal (it is a buff, not a damage zone: DECISIONS_DARK DR5-aura)

M_AF_Telegraph.name: M_AF_Telegraph
M_AF_Telegraph.use: the enemy damage telegraph ground decal (U2 AbyssTelegraphs: EvTelegraph shape / start / contact / style; EvHazard zones in the hazard style, EvArena boundaries in the arena style). One pooled ground quad per telegraph, 8 cm over the terrain (the ground-lift rule of the sprite quads), translucent, unlit, no depth fade, sorted over the ground decals

Rim.map: U = arc length along the boundary / RimTileCm; V = (inward distance to the boundary) / RimWidthCm; colour = RimColor x tex.rgb, opacity = tex.a x RimAlpha

Fill.map: world XY / FillTileCm (never the shape's UV, so the grain does not swim with progress); colour = FillColor x (1 - FillGrain x (1 - tex.rgb)) (at full strength the plate edges read as flagstone paving; .3 keeps a grain, not plates)

shapes.ring: d = max(|p - origin| - radius, innerRadius - |p - origin|)
shapes.cone: the circle of radius clipped to |angle(p - origin, dir)| <= arcDeg / 2 (the edges are rim too)
shapes.line: the box origin -> origin + dir x length, half-width width / 2 (rounded far end)

M_AF_Telegraph.progress: Progress = (now - startMs) / (contactMs - startMs), clamped: the fill grows from the origin (circle, cone, ring: radially to Progress x radius; line: along the length to Progress x length) with a bright front band FrontWidthCm wide at its edge; fill alpha lerps FillAlphaStart -> FillAlphaContact (low on purpose: translucency blends in linear light, so bone at alpha .5 over the #3A332D mud already reads as an opaque pale paving that hides the ground). The fill reaches the rim exactly at the contact beat (monsters.md 1.3)
M_AF_Telegraph.urgency: over the last 30 % of the windup the rim alpha pulses x (0.82 + 0.18 sin(2 pi t / 0.18 s))

contact.look: at Progress 1 the fill jumps to FrontColor alpha fillAlpha and the rim to #FF3A48, then everything fades out over fadeMs; the recipe telegraph.contact (or .line / .cone) plays at the same instant for the dust and the rim snap. The fill stays translucent (VFX r5: bone at .26 rising to a .45 flash read as a near-opaque white paving over the ground and the hero's feet at 760-900 ms); the bright front band and the urgency pulse carry the read

elite.note: a second, thinner rim inside: elites telegraph the same hue with more ink

boss.note: bosses: the widest rim, the inner rim, urgency from half the windup

hazard.window: on for the zone's whole damage window: a hazard that follows a windup (the breach-seep's line) keeps its crimson line from the windup's contact until the zone ends (its last tick), fading out over fadeMs — the decal hands over from its windup style, it never drops to violet only while it still hurts
hazard.note: a lingering zone (EvHazard): rim only; what burns inside is the hazard.* recipe

arena.map: the damage is OUTSIDE the boundary (EvArena, e.g. Valdras P3's closing banner ring: 4 % max life per second outside it): Rim V = the OUTWARD distance from the boundary / RimWidthCm, so the scorched line sits on the boundary and the 45-degree hatch band fades outward, into the side that hurts; outside the rim a faint flat wash of RimColor at outerWash.alpha (ramping in over fadeInCm) — no fill sweep, no bone; inside stays clean
arena.note: an arena boundary (EvArena): which side hurts must read without the recipe — crimson rim, hatch facing outward, a faint crimson wash outside; the fire wall on the edge is hazard.banner_ring

M_AF_Telegraph.rules: crimson + bone only — no hero recipe draws a filling ground shape (hue audit fill rule); enemy magic that is not a damage hazard stays breach-violet

M_AF_AshDissolve.name: M_AF_AshDissolve
M_AF_AshDissolve.use: U3 corpses in ash mode: the death pose holds, the body turns to ash and crumbles into a husk that keeps its place for the corpse TTL (20 s), then blows away; Rise reverses it. Applied to every toon slot of the character (the ink hull follows the same mask so no ink floats over dissolved parts)

Noise.map: object-space XZ / 60 cm (R fBm front, G cracks, B per-plate random)

timeline.grey: after the Death clip ends + holdMs: toon colours lerp to AshColor (lit) / AshShade (shade band) over greyMs; emissive markers (violet eyes, seams) go out at the start of the grey
timeline.crumble: then Dissolve 0 -> crumbleTo over crumbleMs: a pixel drops when (B x 0.6 + R x 0.3 + (1 - G) x 0.15 + heightFraction x 0.3) < Dissolve x 1.4 — whole plates (B dominates: ~12 cm flakes, never per-pixel grain), cracks first, upper parts before the lower; the surviving edge band EdgeWidth glows EdgeColor (pale ash, never warm). The recipe corpse.crumble plays at the start of the crumble
timeline.husk: the remaining ~62 % stays (ash-coloured, no ink fade) until the TTL
timeline.expire: at the TTL: Dissolve crumbleTo -> 1 over expireMs + corpse.expire
timeline.burn: corpse.burn (a fire kill / fire over a corpse): the grey starts at once (no holdMs) under the flare and the crumble follows as usual; the husk is unraisable
timeline.rise: monster.raise: Dissolve and grey reverse over the Rise clip's first 60 %

AshnumbTint.name: AshnumbTint
AshnumbTint.use: K6 StatusType::Ashnumb on the hero (stacks 1-5, 6 s, refreshed on hit; the antidote cleanses it): the hero's toon slots grey from the feet up — a band whose top rises with the stacks — plus the status.ashnumb loop (ash flaking off, dust at the feet). Never violet, never a ground decal
AshnumbTint.map: per vertex the height fraction h = z / heroHeight (object space, the feet at 0); band = 1 - smoothstep(top - BandSoftness, top, h) with top = min(BandTopBase + stacks x BandTopPerStack, MaxBandTop) (1 stack: over the boots to mid-shin; 3: the thighs; 5: the hips); toon colour lerps to AshColor where the toon's key light is in its lit bands, AshShade in its shade band (N.L x .5 + .5 < T_SHADE), by band x Strength; an EdgeColor line EdgeWidth tall on the band's top edge (top - EdgeWidth .. top, full strength); the ink hull and held items are untouched. On a renderer without the per-stack band (mobile low) use the StatusTint path: #8A8480 multiply at .25 + .05 x stacks
AshnumbTint.preview: vfx_effects/AshnumbTint/band_stacks*.png (vfx/ashnumb_band.py: this contract as material nodes on the three heroes at 0 / 1 / 3 / 5 stacks, W1 camera, 1080p, march dirt)
AshnumbTint.readNote: art review r1: with the r0 top (stacks x 0.12) one stack was the boots alone, hidden under the warrior's shield and legs at the W1 camera; the base lifts one stack to mid-shin. Reads clearly on the mage's robe and the rogue's leather; on the warrior's pale steel the ash reads darker and warmer (a dull band) and the EdgeColor line marks its top
AshnumbTint.slowAt5: at 5 stacks the hero is also slowed 20 %: status.slow is NOT added (the band at its top is the read; the slow's own frost look is the wrong element)
AshnumbTint.owner: A12 W2 (vfx/fx_recipes_dark.py ASHNUMB); built by the UE status presentation (2G)
